summary.headline: Orchid Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 15% YoY to INR304 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR25 crore, on a merged Dhanuka basis.
summary.overview: Orchid Pharma reported Q1 FY27 on a combined basis after the Dhanuka Laboratories merger (effective 10 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2024), with FY25 and FY26 restated. Revenue from operations rose to INR304 crore from INR263 crore, and gross margin improved about 3 percentage points to 33%. EBITDA rose to INR25 crore from INR10 crore a year earlier. Management described the quarter as mediocre and said recovery would be gradual, with cephalosporin pricing still under pressure from overcapacity. Project milestones for 7-ACA (March 2027) and cefiderocol (commissioning December 2026) were reiterated.

segments.name: Cephalosporin API / core business
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes and pricing fell 15-20% by product in a difficult cephalosporin year. Cefixime faces the most margin pressure, mainly in rest-of-world markets. 7-ACA pricing has been stable for about a year.

segments.name: Exblifep (Cefepime-Enmetazobactam)
segments.commentary: Europe volumes grew about 300% QoQ in Q3 FY26, about 170-175% in Q4 FY26 and about 50% in Q1 FY27. The Russia licence has an estimated 10-year value of about USD178 million, not current revenue. South Africa registration is done and GCC coverage is in place, but Middle East rollout is delayed by regional conflict.

segments.name: AMS (Antimicrobial Stewardship)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR5 crore in Q1 FY27 from Orblicef and other brands. Quarterly EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR50 lakh.

segments.name: NP-NC (Dhanuka Laboratories)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crore in Q1 FY27, against an earlier quarterly run-rate of INR20-25 crore. Management said it would not reach 25% of revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give FY27 YoY revenue growth guidance; it said it hopes for better QoQ sales in H2, when regulated demand is seasonally stronger.
Merger synergies are expected to show initial benefits from FY28.

Cefiderocol: facility commissioning targeted for December 2026, then validation and initial batches in January-March 2027. Indian approval expected 6-9 months after that, subject to a DCGI trial waiver, so around Q3 FY28.
7-ACA (Jammu): first commercial batch targeted by March 2027. Ramp-up to 80-100% utilisation within the first year, with long-term split of 80% captive and 20% third-party sales.

US formulations strategy: guidance still 2030, with annual updates only. Generic ANDA filings from the cefiderocol facility take a few years; some new molecules may be filed by end of next year, with nothing commercial before 2028.
capex_capacity: 7-ACA project capex about INR750 crore, with commissioning and first commercial batch targeted by March 2027.
Cefiderocol project capex about USD20-25 million; facility commissioning by December 2026.
Management said FY27 capex is not significantly large beyond completing the 7-ACA and cefiderocol projects.
Equipment originally sourced from China was rerouted through Italy, adding execution complexity without changing timelines.

Jammu site chosen for low power costs, abundant water and cheap steam from agricultural waste, plus GST benefit. PLI incentive expected for 2 years, with extension to be sought after the plant starts.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry still has overcapacity and cutthroat competition in non-regulated markets.

7-ACA weighted average price about USD60/kg per management, stable over 10-12 years. 7-ACA supply is concentrated among 3-4 Chinese producers (Sinopharm Weiqida, Zhuhai United, Yili Pharmaceutical, Livzon named).
Cefixime is under the most margin stress, driven by rest-of-world volumes.
Management expects regulated-market demand to improve over the next 2-3 quarters, with H2 seasonally stronger.
Ceftriaxone non-sterile supply from the new 7-ACA-linked capacity is planned for other Indian sterile manufacturers, which currently import from China.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover in H2 FY27 or only in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-regulated competition will persist and is hard to predict. It hopes regulated demand improves over the next two to three quarters, and called Q1 mediocre.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 7-ACA ramp-up and captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up to 80-100% by the end of year one, starting slowly. Long-term guidance is 80% in-house and 20% third-party. All output goes in-house until customer GMP approvals are obtained.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant new capex beyond completing 7-ACA (INR750 crore) and cefiderocol (USD20-25 million).

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth reach about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not be prudent to give an annual growth number at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Exblifep partner pipeline and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Advanced talks for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco and Australia. Management does not guide yearly numbers; the USD1-2 billion is lifetime potential. Management hopes for three or four more agreements by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of Chinese 7-ACA price cuts once the plant is running?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese producers have stable pricing and no cartel-like Pen G situation, so it sees little room for drastic cuts. It also acknowledged that Chinese pricing is unpredictable and that the company is working on yield and tighter concentration as its plan A.

risks_watch: Cephalosporin pricing pressure: management says non-regulated competition persists and is hard to predict; Cefixime margins are under the most stress, driven by rest-of-world volumes.

7-ACA Jammu execution: first commercial batch targeted by March 2027, ramp-up to 80-100% within year one is described as unpredictable and could run longer, with output captive until customer GMP approvals.
Cefiderocol India approval depends on a DCGI clinical trial waiver; approval is expected 6-9 months after commissioning, around Q3 FY28, and the waiver outcome is unknown until application.
Exblifep Middle East rollout delayed by regional conflict; Russia's INR/USD178 million value is a 10-year estimate with registration and launch taking about 1.5-2 years.
Chinese 7-ACA pricing could change; management acknowledged Chinese pricing is unpredictable, and merger synergies and mix gains are expected to show from FY28.
Management declined FY27 growth guidance and said Q1 is mediocre, so H2 regulated-market recovery is unproven; NP-NC Q1 revenue was not split from the INR350 crore total on the call.
key_quotes: And I would consider this quarter as a mediocre in that terms.
So, we hope in the next two, three quarters our demand for the regulated products will improve, and we can do better performance.
I don't think it will be prudent to give you any number at this time.

But for us, what is important is the regulated market demand, which also is kind of cyclical, and we have seen that the quarter where we have more of the regulated products demand, that is much better.
summary.management_tone: Management was cautious and guarded: it called Q1 mediocre, said recovery would be gradual and declined to give FY27 growth or margin numbers. It was more confident on the 7-ACA cost position and Exblifep Europe volume growth, while evading or deferring on Russia timelines, the US filing plan and the Chinese pricing risk.
